name: Angular
summary: Google's full framework for building large web apps with TypeScript, with routing and forms included.
watchOutFor: More to learn than lighter frameworks.
Heavier than needed for a simple site.

name: Anime.js
summary: A lightweight JavaScript animation library for CSS properties, SVG and DOM elements.
strengths: small and easy to start with
works with any framework or none
watchOutFor: Fewer React-specific helpers than some libraries.
Follow the current docs because the API changed between versions.

name: Astro
summary: A web framework for fast, content-focused sites that can still use React and other tools.
strengths: fast, mostly static sites for content
using React or other tools only where needed
watchOutFor: It is less suited to apps with many interactive screens.
You still need some HTML and command-line comfort.

name: Auth0
summary: A hosted identity service for sign-in, with support for many login methods and company accounts.
strengths: a mature service with many sign-in options
support for company and enterprise logins
watchOutFor: It can be complex to configure.
Costs can rise with the number of users.

name: Auth.js
summary: An open-source library that adds sign-in with Google, GitHub, email and other providers to a web app.
strengths: open-source sign-in with no per-user fee
watchOutFor: You manage more of the set-up yourself.
Security details matter. Follow the documentation closely.

name: Better Auth
summary: An open-source TypeScript library for adding sign-in, sessions and plug-ins to your own app.
strengths: you keep the user data in your own database
watchOutFor: You are responsible for configuring it safely.
A newer library. Follow the current docs.

name: Bootstrap
summary: A long-running CSS and JavaScript framework with ready layouts and components.
watchOutFor: Sites can look alike without changes.
Heavier than a few custom styles.

name: Botpress
summary: A platform for building AI chatbots and agents for websites and messaging apps with a visual editor.
strengths: visual builder with AI knowledge sources
watchOutFor: Usage-based costs can add up. Check the pricing page.
Test answers carefully before going public.

name: Carrd
summary: A simple builder for one-page sites such as portfolios, link pages and landing pages.
strengths: very quick for a one-page site
watchOutFor: One page only on most plans.
Some features are paid. Check the current rules.

name: Cashfree Payments
summary: An Indian payment gateway and payouts service for businesses and developers.
watchOutFor: Check fees and settlement times.
Real payments need business verification.

name: Chatbase
summary: A no-code tool that builds a chatbot from your documents and website pages and embeds it on your site.
strengths: a bot from your own files, fast
watchOutFor: Answers are only as good as the content you give it.
Message limits depend on the plan. Check the pricing page.

name: Clerk
summary: A hosted sign-in service with ready-made sign-up and account screens for web apps.
watchOutFor: Free limits and per-user costs can change.
Your users' accounts live on its service.

name: Cloudflare Pages
summary: A hosting service from Cloudflare that publishes static and server-rendered sites from Git.
strengths: hosting on a large global network
a custom domain next to Cloudflare's other tools
watchOutFor: Some Next.js features need extra set-up.
Check the free limits before you rely on it.

name: Contentful
summary: A hosted content platform for teams, where content is stored separately and delivered to sites and apps by API.
watchOutFor: Aimed at larger projects.
Free use is limited. Check the current rules.

name: Microsoft Copilot Studio
summary: Microsoft's low-code tool for building chat agents that connect to Microsoft 365 and other business data.
strengths: connects to business data and workflows
watchOutFor: Mostly aimed at organisations with Microsoft accounts.
Licensing is complex. Check the official page.

name: daisyUI
summary: A plugin for Tailwind CSS that adds ready-made component styles and themes, including dark mode.
strengths: component styles through simple class names
built-in colour themes, including dark mode
watchOutFor: It needs Tailwind CSS set up first.
Themes can make sites look alike.

name: Dify
summary: An open-source platform for building AI apps and chat agents, with a visual workflow editor and a hosted option.
watchOutFor: Self-hosting needs server skills.
Check what data each connected model receives.

name: Django
summary: A Python web framework with an admin panel, database tools and sign-in included.
strengths: a lot included, such as admin and auth
watchOutFor: You need to know Python.
More structure than a small script needs.

name: Expo
summary: A toolset built on React Native for making Android and iOS apps with JavaScript.
strengths: building phone apps with React skills
testing on your own phone quickly
watchOutFor: Publishing to app stores has its own steps and fees.
It suits mobile apps, not ordinary websites.

name: FastAPI
summary: A Python framework for building APIs quickly, with automatic documentation.
watchOutFor: You need to know Python.
It is for APIs, not a full website builder.

name: Firebase
summary: Google's app platform with a database, sign-in, file storage and hosting.
strengths: quick set-up for web and mobile apps
database, sign-in and hosting in one place
watchOutFor: Costs can grow with usage. Set budget alerts.
Data is shaped for its own model, which can make later moves harder.

name: Flowise
summary: An open-source visual builder for chat agents and AI workflows that you can run yourself.
strengths: self-host it or use a hosted version
watchOutFor: Self-hosting means you secure and update it.
Do not expose it without sign-in.

name: Flutter
summary: Google's toolkit for building mobile, web and desktop apps from one codebase in Dart.
watchOutFor: You need to learn Dart.
Apps can look different from native ones.

name: Formspree
summary: A service that receives form submissions from a static site and emails them to you.
strengths: a working form on a static site without a server
watchOutFor: Free plans limit the number of submissions.
Add spam protection to the form.

name: Ghost
summary: A publishing platform for blogs and newsletters, which you can host yourself or use as a service.
strengths: made for writing, memberships and newsletters
open source with a hosted option
watchOutFor: Hosted plans are paid.
Self-hosting means you handle updates.

name: Git
summary: The free, open-source tool that records changes to your files so you can go back, compare and share work.
strengths: the standard way to track code changes
works offline on your own computer
watchOutFor: The commands take time to learn.
Never commit passwords or keys.

name: GitHub
summary: The most widely used website for hosting Git repositories, reviewing code and working with others.
strengths: a huge community and many open-source projects
watchOutFor: Repositories can be public. Check before you push private data.
Some features need a paid plan.

name: GitHub Pages
summary: Free-to-start hosting for static sites, published straight from a GitHub repository.
strengths: free hosting for static sites from your repository
no separate account if you already use GitHub
watchOutFor: Static files only. There is no server code.
Check its usage limits and terms.

name: GitLab
summary: A website for hosting Git repositories with built-in issue tracking and automated builds.
strengths: code hosting and automation in one product
can be run on your own server
watchOutFor: More to learn than a simple host.
Some features need a paid plan.

name: Google Analytics
summary: Google's web analytics service that reports who visits a site and what they do there.
strengths: detailed reports on traffic and behaviour
a tool many teams already know
watchOutFor: Many regions require a cookie notice.
The reports can be overwhelming for a small site.

name: Google Forms
summary: A free form builder in Google's office suite that collects answers into a spreadsheet.
strengths: free forms with answers collected in a spreadsheet
no code and nothing to host
watchOutFor: It looks like a Google form unless you style the page around it.
You need a Google account.

name: Google Sites
summary: Google's simple website builder that works inside a Google account, good for basic pages.
strengths: easy to embed Docs, Sheets and Forms
watchOutFor: Limited design control.
Fewer features than full builders.

name: Gradio
summary: A Python library for building quick web interfaces to try machine-learning models.
strengths: a demo interface in a few lines
watchOutFor: Aimed at demos more than full products.
You need to know Python.

name: GSAP
summary: A JavaScript animation library for detailed, timed and scroll-driven animation on web pages.
watchOutFor: The learning curve is steep.
Check the licence terms for your kind of use.

name: Gumroad
summary: A simple platform for creators to sell digital products, memberships and courses.
strengths: very simple for selling a digital product
watchOutFor: Check fees on the official page.
Payout rules differ by country.

name: Hostinger
summary: A budget web hosting company with shared hosting, WordPress hosting and its own website builder.
watchOutFor: Paid plans only, with renewal prices that can differ. Check the terms.
Shared hosting is slower than dedicated options.

name: Hugging Face Spaces
summary: A hosting service for small AI demos and apps built with Gradio, Streamlit or Docker.
watchOutFor: Free hardware is slow and can sleep.
Public spaces can be seen by anyone.

name: JetBrains IDEs
summary: A family of full-featured editors from JetBrains, such as IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm and WebStorm.
strengths: deep help for one language or stack
watchOutFor: Heavier than a simple editor.
Some editions are paid. Check the official page.

name: Keycloak
summary: An open-source identity server for sign-in, single sign-on and user management that you run yourself.
watchOutFor: Needs server skills to run and secure.
More than a small site needs.

name: Landbot
summary: A no-code builder for chatbots and conversational forms on websites and WhatsApp.
watchOutFor: Check plan limits on conversations.
Test every path before launch.

name: Lemon Squeezy
summary: A service for selling digital products and subscriptions that handles sales tax as the seller of record.
strengths: handles tax and invoices for you
watchOutFor: Check payout availability for your country.
Check its current status and terms on the official site.

name: Lottie
summary: A format and player for small vector animations exported from design tools and used on web pages and apps.
strengths: playing animations made by a designer
watchOutFor: Large animations slow down a page.
You still need a tool to make the animation.

name: Mantine
summary: A React component library with many components and hooks for forms, dates and notifications.
strengths: a large set of components and hooks
watchOutFor: React only.
You need to follow its set-up for your framework.

name: Matomo
summary: A privacy-focused web analytics tool that you can self-host or use as a hosted service.
watchOutFor: Hosted plans are paid.
Self-hosting means you handle updates.

name: Microsoft Clarity
summary: A free tool from Microsoft that shows heatmaps and recordings of how people use a site.
strengths: easy to add to a site
watchOutFor: Recordings can capture sensitive data. Mask forms.
Tell visitors in your privacy policy.

name: MongoDB Atlas
summary: A hosted document database from MongoDB, where data is stored as flexible JSON-like records.
watchOutFor: Check free tier limits before relying on it.
Flexible data still needs a plan to stay tidy.

name: Motion
summary: An animation library for React and JavaScript, formerly known as Framer Motion.
watchOutFor: Heavy motion slows pages. Respect reduced-motion settings.
You need to know basic React.

name: MUI
summary: A large library of ready-made React components, previously known as Material UI.
strengths: a large, mature set of components
watchOutFor: The default look is easy to recognise. Customise it.
Some advanced components may be paid.

name: Neon
summary: A hosted Postgres database that scales to zero when idle and supports branching.
strengths: standard Postgres with a generous start
watchOutFor: Free use is limited. Check the current rules.
Idle databases may pause and wake slowly.

name: Netlify
summary: A hosting service that publishes a site from a folder or a Git repository, with built-in form handling.
strengths: publishing by dragging a folder in
watchOutFor: Free plans have bandwidth and form limits.
Check the terms if the site earns money.

name: Next.js
summary: A React framework for building websites and web apps with pages, routing and server features.
strengths: routing, rendering and a large ecosystem
watchOutFor: You need to know React first.
Its server features take time to learn.

name: Node.js
summary: A JavaScript runtime that runs code outside the browser, used for servers and build tools.
strengths: JavaScript on the server and for tooling
watchOutFor: It is a runtime, not a web framework.
Install only from the official site.

name: Payload
summary: An open-source headless CMS and app framework built with TypeScript, that fits into a Next.js project.
watchOutFor: Aimed at developers.
You host and update it yourself.

name: PayPal
summary: A widely known service for online payments and checkout buttons, used by buyers and sellers worldwide.
watchOutFor: Availability and rules depend on your country.
Check fees on the official pricing page.

name: Paytm Payment Gateway
summary: Paytm's payment gateway for Indian businesses, supporting UPI, cards, wallets and net banking.
strengths: a brand many Indian customers know
watchOutFor: Business sign-up and approval rules apply.
Check fees and settlement terms with the provider.

name: PayU
summary: An Indian payment gateway that accepts cards, netbanking, UPI and wallets.
strengths: an established gateway for Indian merchants
watchOutFor: Check fees and onboarding steps.
Real payments need business verification.

name: PhonePe Payment Gateway
summary: PhonePe's payment gateway for Indian businesses, supporting UPI, cards and wallets on websites and apps.
strengths: a brand many Indian customers know
watchOutFor: Business sign-up and approval rules apply.
Check fees and settlement terms with the provider.

name: Plausible
summary: A simple, privacy-focused web analytics service that shows key numbers on one page.
strengths: one simple page of key numbers
watchOutFor: The hosted service may be paid. Self-hosting is possible.
It is less detailed than larger tools.

name: PocketBase
summary: An open-source back end in a single file, with a database, sign-in, file storage and an admin screen.
watchOutFor: You host it yourself.
Still changing quickly before version 1.

name: PostgreSQL
summary: A powerful, free, open-source database used for everything from small apps to large systems.
watchOutFor: Running it yourself needs server skills.
A hosted service is simpler for beginners.

name: PostHog
summary: An analytics platform with page views, funnels, session replay and feature flags, hosted or self-hosted.
strengths: open source with a hosted option
watchOutFor: Free use is limited. Check the current rules.
A lot of features for a simple site.

name: Radix UI
summary: Unstyled, accessible building blocks for React such as dialogs, menus and tabs that you style yourself.
watchOutFor: You write the styles.
React only.

name: Railway
summary: A hosting platform for apps and databases with a simple dashboard and Git deploys.
strengths: quick to deploy apps and databases
watchOutFor: Usage-based costs. Set limits.
Check current free options.

name: Razorpay
summary: An Indian payment gateway for UPI, cards and netbanking, with no-code payment links and developer tools.
strengths: UPI, cards and netbanking for Indian customers
payment links that need no code
watchOutFor: You need to complete business verification before taking real payments.
Check fees and settlement times.

name: React
summary: A JavaScript library for building interactive user interfaces from reusable components.
strengths: a huge community and many tutorials
watchOutFor: It is a library, not a full framework. You choose routing and structure yourself.
Beginners face many setup choices.

name: Render
summary: A hosting platform for websites, back ends and databases that deploys from a Git repository.
strengths: supports static sites, servers and databases
watchOutFor: Free services may sleep when idle.
Check current free limits.

name: Sanity
summary: A hosted content system with an editing studio that you shape to fit your content.
strengths: a hosted service with nothing to run yourself
watchOutFor: A developer needs to set up the editing studio.
Free limits and plans may change.

name: shadcn/ui
summary: A set of accessible React interface components that you copy into your project and change freely.
strengths: components you own and can change freely
watchOutFor: It expects React and Tailwind CSS.
Left unchanged, every site built with it looks alike.

name: Shopify
summary: A platform for building and running an online shop, with payments, shipping and apps.
watchOutFor: Paid subscription with a trial listed on the official page.
Apps and transaction fees add to the cost.

name: SQLite
summary: A small, free database that lives in a single file, used in apps, phones and browsers.
watchOutFor: Not meant for many writers at once.
Back it up as you would any file.

name: Squarespace
summary: A website builder known for polished templates, with hosting, domains and simple shops built in.
strengths: hosting and a domain in one place
watchOutFor: Paid subscription with a trial listed on the official page.
Moving your site elsewhere later can be hard.

name: Strapi
summary: An open-source content system you run yourself, with a ready admin panel and an API.
strengths: an admin panel without writing one
open source, so you control your data
watchOutFor: Self-hosting means you run and secure the server.
A hosted version, if you want one, is a paid service.

name: Streamlit
summary: A Python library for turning scripts into simple web apps for data and AI demos.
strengths: a web app from a Python script
quick for data dashboards and demos
watchOutFor: Limited control over layout.
You need to know Python.

name: Stripe
summary: A payments platform for taking cards and subscriptions online, with strong developer tools.
watchOutFor: Availability depends on your country and business type.
Check fees on the official pricing page.

name: Supabase
summary: An open-source back end that offers a Postgres database, sign-in and file storage.
strengths: a full database with sign-in built in
an open-source base you can move away from
watchOutFor: Learn its access rules before storing private data.
Free projects may pause when unused.

name: SvelteKit
summary: A framework for building websites and apps with Svelte, with routing and server rendering built in.
strengths: less code for the same interface
watchOutFor: A smaller ecosystem than React.
Fewer ready-made libraries.

name: Tailwind CSS
summary: A CSS framework of small utility classes that you combine to style a page directly in your markup.
watchOutFor: Class names can get long. Learn it before a big project.
It styles. It does not give you ready components.

name: Tally
summary: A simple form builder that works like a document, with a generous free start for surveys and sign-ups.
strengths: build a form like a document
watchOutFor: Some features need a paid plan.
Check the current free limits.

name: three.js
summary: A JavaScript library for showing 3D scenes in the browser.
strengths: the standard way to do 3D on the web
watchOutFor: 3D code takes time to learn.
Heavy scenes can be slow on phones.

name: Typeform
summary: A form builder that shows one question at a time, for surveys and sign-ups with a friendly feel.
watchOutFor: Free use limits responses. Check the current rules.
Longer forms can feel slow.

name: Umami
summary: An open-source, privacy-focused web analytics tool you can host yourself or use as a service.
watchOutFor: Self-hosting means you run the server and database.
A hosted version may be paid.

name: Vercel
summary: A hosting service that publishes a site from a Git repository and gives each change a preview link.
strengths: a live site on every push to Git
watchOutFor: Free plans can limit commercial use.
Check bandwidth and function limits.

name: Visual Studio Code
summary: A free, extensible code editor from Microsoft, with a large library of extensions, including AI assistants.
strengths: free and works on Windows, macOS and Linux
watchOutFor: You choose and install extensions yourself, so check who publishes each one.
AI features come from extensions and may have their own limits.

name: Vite
summary: A fast build tool and dev server for modern web projects, with templates for React, Vue and others.
watchOutFor: It is a build tool, not a full framework.
You choose routing and data tools yourself.

name: Voiceflow
summary: A collaborative tool for designing and launching chat and voice assistants.
strengths: a visual canvas for conversation flows
watchOutFor: Plans and limits change. Check the pricing page.
Test answers carefully before going public.

name: Vue.js
summary: A JavaScript framework for building web interfaces, known for being easy to pick up.
watchOutFor: A smaller job market than React in some regions.
Pick one set-up and follow its docs.

name: Web3Forms
summary: A form back end that sends submissions from a static site to your email with no server of your own.
strengths: a form back end with no server to run
simple set-up with a key in your form
watchOutFor: Check submission limits on free use.
Add spam protection to the form.

name: WordPress
summary: A widely used open-source system for running a blog or website, with themes and plugins.
strengths: a huge range of themes and plugins
editing posts and pages without code
watchOutFor: Keep plugins and themes updated. Old ones are a security risk.
Hosting is a separate cost.

name: Zed
summary: A fast code editor built for speed and collaboration, with built-in AI features.
strengths: very quick to open and use
built-in AI assistant and real-time collaboration
watchOutFor: Smaller extension library than the biggest editors.
AI features may need an account or your own model keys.
